# dtcloud_volume (Data Source)

Looks up one volume by id.

Use it to reference a volume Terraform did not create -- attaching an existing disk to a new machine, for instance. Declaring it as a resource instead would hand Terraform ownership of it, and a later `terraform destroy` would delete the volume and its snapshots.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "dtcloud_volume" "data" {
  id = var.volume_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) ID of the volume to look up.

### Read-Only

- `attached_to` (String) Name of the VM this volume is attached to.
- `attached_to_id` (String) ID of the VM this volume is attached to.
- `attached_to_status` (String) Status of the VM this volume is attached to.
- `bootable` (Boolean) Whether the volume can be booted from.
- `created` (String) When the volume was created.
- `image_metadata` (List of Object) Details of the image this volume was created from. Empty for a blank volume. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--image_metadata))
- `is_detachable` (Boolean) Whether the platform will allow this volume to be detached.
- `last_modified` (String) When the volume last changed.
- `name` (String) Name of the volume.
- `size` (Number) Size in GB.
- `status` (String) Status reported by the platform.
- `storage_policy` (String) Storage policy backing the volume.
- `volume_type` (String) HDD, or CD-ROM when the volume holds an ISO.

<a id="nestedatt--image_metadata"></a>
### Nested Schema for `image_metadata`

Read-Only:

- `checksum` (String)
- `container_format` (String)

- `image_name` (String)
- `min_disk` (String)
- `min_ram` (String)

- `os_type` (String)
